scope: foundation-cpu selected native skills and Codex/Claude practice on the current Linux/WSL host; user explicitly deferred second-machine acceptance

gates.acceptance: Installed-version upstream source review, native app-server configuration write/readback, isolated apply/rollback; required meaningful local integration checks; exact-version and idle protections retained.
Frozen focused routing cases, actual native skill read/invocation and concrete task outcomes; record all misses, false positives and native failures separately for Codex and Claude.
At least one identical native Claude task with skill discovery enabled and native --disable-slash-commands baseline at the same explicit model/effort. A passing baseline is not a quality gain.

Native Claude Opus at max independently critiques the integrated changes/evidence; adjudicate findings by original pinned sources and actual checks, preserve dissent and failures. Final review has no unresolved blocking source/acceptance finding within the declared scope.
Deferred by the user's explicit 'Finish this host first' answer. Current-host fresh-prefix or hosted smoke cannot count as second-machine acceptance.

Relevant unchanged checks, scoped convergence validator, evidence/catalog validator, generated guide check and whitespace check pass on final inputs; historical upstream tests stay distinct from integration tests.

model_policy.astra_escalation: Consequential architecture, conflicting primary evidence or failure unresolved after one bounded Sol repair; record trigger and acceptance.

state_policy: Do not inspect credential values, kill active clients, bypass idle/version protections or overwrite concurrent owners. Logs and per-host active state remain private; publish compact sanitized receipts.
quality_rule: Qualification is scoped to observed gates. No universal SOTA, all-28 implicit routing, broad superiority or efficiency claim.
usage_rule: Retain per-native-attempt usage once; keep cache subsets separate, failed attempts visible and unknown counters null.
